title: Refocus Foundry: signal-first, agent-ready site layer streaming to Polaris
description:
New direction (operator, 2026-08-20): Foundry is the wireframe for websites that capture ALL signal proving whether the site works — analytics/events (what visitors do, incl. agent traffic) plus an error/warning log stream — and ship it raw to an external consumer (Polaris for us; Grafana-class tools for others). No in-Foundry charts/dashboards; anomaly detection lives in the consumer. Decision-log is OUT of product scope (resolves the CHOPPING-BLOCK.md vision tension). Second pillar: agent-readiness — agentic traffic will dwarf human traffic, so the site must be discoverable/interactable by agents (MCP + llms.txt kept, reversing Tier-1 cut) alongside strong SEO. Opinionated design/layout is de-prioritized: AI makes design cheap, we should not hard-code it.

DECIDED CUTS: KaTeX/math pipeline; changelog module; OgImageDocs (keep OgImageLanding); webhook notification formatters (discord/slack/telegram + retry + anti-spam machinery) — replaced by the unified Polaris signal channel; evlog probably out unless it materially eases the Polaris connection (decision task).

DECIDED KEEPS: MCP server tools + nuxt-llms (agent discoverability); SEO stack; events module (main focus, rearchitected); convert components (intent signal); nuxt-studio; team collection; motion-v; surround prev/next; fuse.js; content collections (pages/faq/config/navigation). Infra modules (config, css, markdown-rewrite, useAppStorage, useUserIdentity): selective audit.

Ref: strategy/CHOPPING-BLOCK.md

Signal buffer + authenticated export live with 33 signal tests; errors/warnings captured; visitor classification shipped; notification machinery, evlog drain surface, orphaned MCP tools, dead docs remnants, and non-minimal sections removed; VISION.md rewritten (schema v3, draft — awaiting operator approval); stale epic tree reconciled; Polaris-side epic filed (polaris-kaf). title: UPageHero hydration mismatch causes 0.10 CLS on content-driven pages
description:
Default layout's UPageHero v-if reads context.page, which is null when the layout's render function runs during SSR (layout setup completes BEFORE the catch-all page's setup populates context via setContext). Result: SSR emits a v-if comment, client hydration populates context and renders a 448px tall hero, body container shifts from y=84 to y=532. CLS=0.102 on /render-landing, 0.076 on /render-default. Article layout has a related UPageHeader SSR/CSR mismatch (filed separately). App-page versions of the same layouts CLS=0.000.

Root cause: in Vue's slot model, layouts render their own template before the page setup inside <slot/> resolves. Layouts that read page-derived state will always disagree between SSR and CSR.

Fix: move UPageHero out of the layout, into pages/[...slug].vue (above ContentRenderer). Layouts become pure presentation chrome; page-derived UI lives next to the content it describes.

title: routeRules.appLayout has no effect — layout still resolves to default
description: Setting routeRules: { '/foo': { appLayout: 'article' } } in nuxt.config.ts does not switch the rendered layout. /foo still resolves through the default layout (and 404s because default.vue requires content). Need to either (a) wire a route middleware that reads to.meta.appLayout from the rule and calls setPageLayout(), or (b) rely on Nuxt 4 native support if it exists in 4.4.2 — currently it does not appear to.\n\nAstronera depends on this in nuxt.config.ts:34-50 — if their pages work, it's because they also ship the matching layout files in app/layouts/.
close_reason: Closed

title: Default layout hard-404s any route without a matching content/pages file
description: layer/app/layouts/default.vue:11 throws createError({statusCode:404,fatal:true}) when useContentPage().getPage() returns null. Effect: every app/pages/*.vue that doesn't have a sibling content/pages/*.md returns 404 unless it sets definePageMeta({layout:false}). Both incubrain and astronera work around this by setting layout:false on every app page they author — but the bug means the 'default' layout is unusable for app pages and only the catch-all + content can use it.\n\nFix options: (1) only throw 404 when route is matched by the catch-all (check route.matched), or (2) make the 404 throw conditional on a layout prop, or (3) move getPage() into the catch-all page component and let layouts be content-agnostic.
close_reason: Closed

title: Rendering & routing architecture sync
description:
Items that touch *what gets rendered at which URL*. Relevant to our catch-all + route-rules + content-driven setup.

- v5.6.0 landing: make it optional (#1274)
- v5.6.0 layer: handle docs prefix & folder (#1275)
- v5.6.1 layer: root docs prefix fix (#1283)
- v5.5.0 llms: redirect homepage to /llms.txt (#1263)
- v5.5.0 llms: docs page → raw markdown for agents (#1264)
- v5.8.0 nav: opt-in sub-navigation (#1298)
- v5.10.0 layer: forward defaultVariants to subcomponents (#1338)
- v5.11.0 layer: ContentTOC default variant 'circuit' (#1360)
- v5.11.0 toc: wider main grid (#1363)

Approach: review each PR diff against our nuxt.config route rules + catch-all routing before adopting. Goal is to preserve our template flexibility.
notes:
Resolution (2026-05-20):

Investigation found upstream's rendering pattern is LESS flexible than ours, not more.

Comparison:
- Ours: catch-all is layout-agnostic; layout fetches data via useContentPage(); layout selection via routeRules.appLayout (declarative). Supports 4+ layouts on the same catch-all.
- Upstream: catch-all locked to a single layout via definePageMeta({layout:'docs'}); page does fetching; only default + docs layouts; filesystem auto-detection of landing/docs prefix.

Dispositions:
- #1274 landing optional → skip (already-equivalent via routeRules)
- #1275 docs prefix & folder → skip (filesystem auto-detect conflicts with our content-first explicit config)
- #1283 root docs prefix fix → skip (we don't have the bug)
- #1263 homepage llms.txt redirect → skip (clashes with landing; nuxt-llms already handles llms.txt)
- #1264 raw markdown redirects → moved to new bd issue (Vercel-only, orthogonal)
- #1338 forward defaultVariants → adopted (added highlight:true to contentNavigation in layer/app/app.config.ts)
- #1298 sub-navigation → moved to .5 investigate
- #1360 ContentTOC circuit → moved to .5 investigate
- #1363 wider TOC grid → moved to .5 investigate
close_reason: Resolved — see final note. Our rendering pattern is more flexible than upstream's; one small variant default adopted, three items moved to .5, one to new sibling issue.

title: Ratify the Foundry→Polaris signal transport design
description: Proposed (see session brainstorm, 2026-08-20): PULL model. Polaris is local-first (desktop/Tauri, later mobile) and not publicly addressable, so push-webhooks from public Foundry sites cannot reach it without an always-on relay. Instead: each Foundry site buffers a unified signal stream server-side and exposes an authenticated cursor-based export endpoint (GET /api/_signals/export?since=<cursor>, bearer token minted per-site in Polaris). Polaris server polls on its scheduler, appends per-site JSONL (its existing durable-store discipline), dedupes by event id, mines anomalies locally. Envelope: {id, ts, site, kind: event|log, name|category, severity?, visitor:{anonId, class: human|agent|bot}, page, referrer, utm, data}. Buffer via Nitro unstorage (fs driver on Railway/Docker, KV driver on Vercel, memory in dev), capped ring buffer (~10k rows / 7d). Grafana-class consumers use the same endpoint or a later generic push drain — envelope stays provider-neutral. Confirm or amend before implementation tasks start.
close_reason: Ratified as proposed: pull model. Foundry site buffers unified signal envelope server-side (unstorage, capped ring buffer), exposes GET /api/_signals/export?since=<cursor> with per-site bearer token; Polaris polls on its scheduler, appends per-site JSONL, dedupes by id, mines anomalies locally. Operator approved by directing execution 2026-08-20.

title: Real external founders run the loop and the first fundable candidate surfaces

# Real external founders run the loop and the first fundable candidate surfaces

## Milestone (this quarter's slice of the vision)
Prove the mechanism with real users: get a cohort of external founders through the loop via a hackathon, and surface the first fundable candidate to Drew via a deal-flow view built on their decision data. This is the validated-mechanism milestone — the true 1-3yr "done."

## Vision-source
> Done at horizon = founders reach go/no-go in <2 weeks at a scale of hundreds→thousands, with 5-10% funded through Drew or his connections. Failure = popular free Carrd surfacing zero data/funding. The realistic 1-3yr slice is the validated mechanism: ≥1 real external founder surfaces as fundable.

## What done looks like
- **[2027Q1] First hackathon cohort** (`product-validator-3so`) — N real external founders through the template.
- **[2027Q1] Deal-flow dashboard (for you)** (`product-validator-36z`) — surface fundable candidates from decision data; begin the 5-10% test.

## Cross-quarter dependencies
- Depends on: `2026q4-foundry-data-loop-and-funnel` (need funnel site + consent data loop live before any outreach).
- Unblocks: Phase D (scale + funded conversion) — not filed this cycle; surfaces at a future `/ib:goals`.

## Out of scope (this quarter)
- Scale to hundreds/thousands of founders — Phase D, beyond this horizon.
- University outreach push — descoped from the default; revisit at quarter planning if hackathon signal is strong.
- Heuristic hardening from founder data — descoped from default; fold into the deal-flow work if cheap.

## Heuristics honoured
- [[working-first]] — one real cohort + one surfaced candidate beats a polished pipeline with no users.

## How we'll know it worked
At least one real external founder (not Drew) runs the full loop and shows up in the deal-flow view as a genuine investment candidate. Many users but zero fundable signal = the vision's named failure mode, not success.

title: The consent-based data flywheel turns, and foundry has a public front door
description:
# The consent-based data flywheel turns, and foundry has a public front door

## Milestone (this quarter's slice of the vision)
Build the moat ingredient — a consent-based Claude plugin that forwards anonymized founder decision-data to incubrain and mirrors it back to the founder as growth feedback — and productize the `examples/` boilerplate into foundry's public front door, with the data deal stated openly.

## Vision-source
> The moat is a data flywheel: more founders → more consent-based decision data → sharper heuristics + diligence → better picks and a productisable system. The data is mirrored back to the founder as growth feedback (C-frame); the system is free because that anonymized data trains it (A-frame). Silent, ToS-buried extraction is consciously refused — it would burn the credibility flywheel.

## What done looks like
- **[2026Q4] Consent data forwarder (Claude plugin)** (`product-validator-puo`) — the moat; anonymized decision-data → incubrain.
- **[2026Q4] Mirror-back growth feedback** (`product-validator-09v`) — data surfaced to the founder as their own product.
- **[2026Q4] Marketing/funnel site** (`product-validator-a8b`) — `examples/` boilerplate → public front door + template.
- **[2026Q4] Consent / how-it-works page** (`product-validator-5x1`) — states the data deal up front (anti-B-frame).

## Cross-quarter dependencies
- Depends on: `2026q3-foundry-integrated-founder-loop` (the forwarder builds on the decision log).
- Unblocks: `2027q1-foundry-first-external-founders` (need the funnel + consent loop live before outreach).

## Out of scope (this quarter)
- External founder cohorts / outreach — deferred to 2027Q1.
- Deal-flow dashboard — deferred to 2027Q1: needs data flowing first.

## Heuristics honoured
- [[best-part-is-no-part]] — the consent page and how-it-works may be one surface.
- [[modular-entrypoints]] — the forwarder, the mirror, and the funnel site are independent entry points.

## How we'll know it worked
Anonymized decision-data from a real loop run reaches incubrain *and* is visible to the founder as growth feedback, and foundry has a public URL a stranger could land on and understand the deal. If data flows but the founder can't see their own mirror — or the consent isn't stated up front — the milestone is not met (it would be the B-frame the vision forbids).

# A founder can go idea → grilled thesis → live signal-capture page (dogfooded)

## Milestone (this quarter's slice of the vision)
Stand up Phase A's core: a founder is grilled from a vague idea into a sharp thesis + a concrete validation plan with go/no-go criteria, and that output wires into the existing layer to produce a live signal-capture page, with decisions persisted as a credibility artifact. Proven by running Drew's own next idea fully through the loop.

## Vision-source
> A Pune serial-attempt founder opens foundry, spends ~1 day being AI-grilled from vague idea → sharp thesis + validation plan, ships a zero-setup signal-capturing page, and runs a data-guided loop that helps them quit early, pivot early, validate early, build fast — reaching go/no-go in <2 weeks. The decision log that falls out is simultaneously their credibility artifact and incubrain's deal-flow funnel.

## What done looks like
- **[2026Q3] Founder grilling flow (idea→thesis)** (`product-validator-ufs`) — the core day-1 experience; reuses the harness grilling engine.
- **[2026Q3] Validation-plan + go/no-go output** (`product-validator-7gb`) — grill emits concrete plan + kill criteria.
- **[2026Q3] Wire grill → live signal-capture page** (`product-validator-iau`) — end-to-end loop via existing layer.
- **[2026Q3] Decision-log capture + display** (`product-validator-kj3`) — decisions surfaced via existing RSS/MCP.

## Cross-quarter dependencies
- Unblocks: `2026q4-foundry-data-loop-and-funnel` (the consent data forwarder builds on the decision log).

## Out of scope (this quarter)

title: 10 pre-existing typecheck errors block pnpm verify (release gate)
description:
The release-it before:init hook runs pnpm verify which includes pnpm typecheck. Typecheck fails with 10 pre-existing errors unrelated to recent changes — h3 v1/v2 conflicts and a few property-access issues:

- app/utils/prerender.ts (4x): event.node possibly undefined
- modules/docs/runtime/layouts/docs.vue (2x): Property 'toc' does not exist on type {}
- modules/rss/server/routes/rss/[collection].ts (2x): H3Event h3@1 vs h3@2 mismatch
- server/mcp/tools/list-pages.ts: H3Event h3@1 vs h3@2 mismatch
- server/middleware/docs-redirect.ts: event.node possibly undefined

0.7.0 must have shipped past this gate somehow (skipping verify, or these crept in after). Need to either:
(a) Fix the actual issues — narrow event.node access, type the docs toc, choose one h3 version, OR
(b) Decide verify is too strict and remove typecheck from the pre-release gate, OR
(c) Skip pnpm verify for the 0.7.1 release with a known-issue acknowledgement.

The h3 ones tie back to the deferred Nitro v3 / h3@2 / unhead@3 cascade (blocks @nuxtjs/seo 5.1.3 + evlog 2.17.0).

title: Set up verdaccio local-registry workflow for testing layer changes in external consumers
description:
Need a way to test local foundry layer changes against external consumer repos (astronera, incubrain) before publishing to npm. pnpm's link: protocol doesn't work cleanly cross-repo: link target keeps its own dep tree in the source repo, and ESM resolution can't cross pnpm's strict isolation boundary. Cross-repo workspaces work but break each consumer's independence.

Verdaccio gives a local npm registry. Workflow: pnpm publish layer to localhost:4873 with @local tag → consumer does pnpm add @incubrain/foundry@local --registry http://localhost:4873 → tarball flows through normal pnpm install with full transitive resolution.

Deliverables:
- publish:local script in layer/package.json (version bump + publish + reset)
- recipe in AGENTS.md for consumers (astronera, incubrain) to add foundry:local / foundry:remote scripts
- pre-commit guard recipe (simple-git-hooks) blocking commits of the @local spec
- smoke-test the loop end-to-end
- verdaccio install: brew or docker, document both
close_reason: Closed

title: UPageHeader SSR/CSR text-node mismatch in article layout
description: Hydration warning: 'Hydration node mismatch ... expected on client: Symbol(v-txt) ... at <UPageHeader>'. Likely caused by Nuxt UI v4 emitting comment placeholders SSR-side for slot content that the client re-emits as text nodes. Same family as UPageHero CLS bug. Investigate together once that fix lands.

title: CommentToggle component reference broken in AppHeaderRight
description: layer/app/components/app/header/AppHeaderRight.vue references <CommentToggle> but the component is not registered/imported. Vue logs '[Vue warn]: Failed to resolve component: CommentToggle' on every page load. Either register the missing component or remove the tag.

title: @nuxt/content 3.13 SSR query fails under h3@1: event.req.headers.entries is not a function
description:
When the layer's catch-all calls queryCollection('pages').path(...).first() during SSR, the auto-imported client queryCollection performs an HTTP roundtrip via event.$fetch('/__nuxt_content/<collection>/query'). Under our pinned h3@1 + @nuxt/content@3.13, that internal fetch throws 'event.req.headers.entries is not a function' because content expects h3 v2 Web Headers but Nitro on h3@1 still uses Node-style header objects.

This silently swallows the error inside useAsyncData and returns null → catch-all 404s for every content URL during SSR in dev.

Workaround applied: useContentPage.getPage now uses @nuxt/content/server's queryCollection(event, ...) directly when import.meta.server. Bypasses the HTTP layer entirely on server. Real fix is to upgrade h3 to v2, which cascades into unhead@3 + nuxt-seo@5.1.3 — currently blocked by other peer conflicts.
close_reason: Closed

title: useContentPage drops content for '/' route (trailing-slash bug)
description: useContentPage.ts:65-67 normalizes route.path by stripping a trailing slash. For route.path='/' this yields '', then queryCollection('pages').path('').first() returns null and the catch-all renders nothing → 404 for the root URL of any Foundry consumer that relies on content/pages/index.md instead of an app-page index.vue. Both incubrain and astronera bypass this by shipping an app/pages/index.vue.\n\nFix: special-case '/'. e.g. path === '/' ? '/' : path.replace(/\\/$/, '').
close_reason: Closed

title: Page rendering test matrix in playground
description: Comprehensive E2E rendering tests in playground covering SSR/SPA/SSG/catch-all/layout-precedence/routeRules. Mirrors real-world patterns from incubrain (layout:false app pages, noindex internal) and astronera (ssr:false /viirs/**, routeRules.appLayout, custom layouts). Includes doc page at examples/foundry/content/docs/ explaining the rendering model. Uses @nuxt/test-utils setup() + nuxi generate smoke test.

title: Sync upstream docus changes since fork (v5.4.4 → v5.11.0)
description:
# Upstream Docus Sync — Diff Report

**Baseline:** docus `v5.4.4` (2026-01-19) — pinned to our hard-fork commit `97ecc15` (2026-01-25).
**Upstream HEAD:** `v5.11.0` (2026-05-07).
**Releases reviewed:** 11 (v5.5.0 → v5.11.0).
**Method:** Option A — changelog skim (`/Users/mac/.opensrc/repos/github.com/nuxt-content/docus/main/CHANGELOG.md`).

## Triage legend

- **ADOPT** — fits our scope (`layer/modules/docs/`), low risk, clear value.
- **INVESTIGATE** — relevant area; needs a code-level look before adopt/skip.
- **SKIP** — out of scope (AI assistant, i18n, MCP, OIDC) or theme-only choices we don't share.

## Shortlist (ADOPT)

| # | Release | Change | PR | Rationale |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | v5.8.0 | fix(typescript): support `nuxt typecheck` in apps extending docus | #1300 | We run `pnpm typecheck` — likely fixes the same edge cases for our layer extenders. |
| 2 | v5.5.0 | feat(layer): `sitemap.xml` generation | #1259 | SEO win for docs; aligns with our content-first stance. |
| 3 | v5.5.0 | fix(layer): enhance sitemap generation, exclude navigation files | #1261 | Pairs with #2. |
| 4 | v5.5.0 | feat(llms): redirect docs pages to raw markdown for agents | #1264 | Agent-friendly; cheap to port. |
| 5 | v5.5.1 | feat(layer): more SEO optimization | #1267 | SEO. |
| 6 | v5.5.1 | fix(docs): don't show separator if github disabled | #1270 | Small UX bug; we likely have it. |
| 7 | v5.6.0 | fix(layer): use native sqlite connector | 33334ce | Perf/build hygiene; matches our `better-sqlite3` setup. |
| 8 | v5.7.0 | fix(layer): improve og image generation | #1286 | SEO. |
| 9 | v5.9.0 | feat(ogImage): upgrade to v6 + use primary color | #1312 | OG/SEO refresh. |
| 10 | v5.9.0 | fix(og): set og image as static | #1324 | Stability. |
| 11 | v5.9.0 | fix(og): limit description size | #1325 | SEO correctness. |
| 12 | v5.9.0 | feat(layer): option to force color-mode | #1310 | Useful escape hatch for docs site. |
| 13 | v5.9.0 | fix(layer): don't display edit page if github url missing | #1327 | Small UX fix. |
| 14 | v5.10.0 | fix(build): remove noisy vite warns | #1344 | DX win. |
| 15 | v5.11.0 | feat(css): support `app/app.css` to avoid duplicate tailwind | #1364 | Build hygiene; we share tailwind across layer + example. |
| 16 | v5.11.0 | fix(css): don't use `@layer base` for prod hydration | 73606b7 | Hydration correctness; low-risk patch. |

## INVESTIGATE (needs code look)

| # | Release | Change | PR | Why investigate |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| I1 | v5.5.0 | feat: add `skills/` folder + `/create-docs` skill | #1257 | We already have `skills/docs-writer/`; check if upstream pattern is worth converging on. |
| I2 | v5.5.0 | feat(llms): redirect homepage to `/llms.txt` | #1263 | Strong opinion; may conflict with our landing. |
| I3 | v5.6.0 | feat(landing): make it optional | #1274 | Could be cleaner config surface for docs-only sites. |
| I4 | v5.6.0 | feat(layer): handle docs prefix & folder | #1275 | We hardcode docs path; this would generalize it. |
| I5 | v5.7.0 | feat(customization): native support for custom icons | #1288 | We swapped `@iconify/json` for individual icon packages (`7fc8ecf`) — see if their approach is better. |
| I6 | v5.8.0 | feat(nav): opt-in sub-navigation | #1298 | Possibly useful for our docs nav module. |
| I7 | v5.10.0 | feat(layer): forward app config defaultVariants to subcomponents | #1338 | Theme propagation — touches our Nuxt UI usage. |
| I8 | v5.11.0 | feat(layer): set `ContentTOC` default variant to `circuit` + wider grid | #1360 #1363 | UI default; check against our docs layout aesthetic. |

## SKIP (out of scope)

- **AI assistant module** — v5.5.0 #1241 and all `assistant:*` follow-ups (v5.5.1, v5.6.0, v5.8.0, v5.9.0, v5.10.1). We removed the assistant during fork; validation ≠ product.
- **MCP / OIDC** — v5.8.0, v5.9.0, v5.10.1, v5.11.0 fixes around MCP tooling and OIDC auth. Not part of our docs surface.
- **i18n** — v5.4.4 #1246, v5.5.0 locale/lazy, v5.6.0 nav transform, v5.8.0 click mode, v5.10.0 nl + missing keys. We explicitly removed i18n (`97ecc15`).
- **`.starters/*` prerendering fixes** — v5.5.0 (3 commits), v5.9.0 #1328, v5.10.0 #1334. We don't ship docus starters.
- **Skills discovery via `.well-known`** — v5.9.0 #1297. Convergence with upstream skills not yet decided (see I1).
- **Right-click and logo handling** — v5.6.1 #1281. UI polish on docus homepage that doesn't map to our docs.

## Suggested adoption order

1. **Group A — DX/build (cheap, low risk):** items 1, 7, 14, 15, 16.
2. **Group B — SEO (high value):** items 2, 3, 5, 8, 9, 10, 11.
3. **Group C — Agent/LLM:** item 4 + decide I2.
4. **Group D — UX polish:** items 6, 12, 13.
5. **Investigate phase:** triage I1–I8 in parallel.

## Caveats

- Changelog descriptions are short; some "fixes" may pull architecture changes. Spot-check each commit before cherry-picking.
- Our `layer/modules/docs/` was heavily restructured during the fork — direct cherry-pick will rarely apply. Expect to **transcribe the change** rather than `git cherry-pick`.
- Path mapping: upstream `layer/app/components/*` → our `layer/modules/docs/runtime/components/*`. Upstream `layer/server/*` → mostly removed in our fork.
acceptance_criteria: All ADOPT items landed or explicitly deferred. All INVESTIGATE items have a decision (adopt or close with reason). Diff report kept up to date as we move closer to upstream HEAD.

title: Fix broken OG component reference in landing layout ('Frame' is not a registered component)
description:
layer/app/layouts/landing.vue line 43 calls defineOgImageComponent('Frame', {...}). No component named 'Frame' (or 'OgImageFrame') exists in the layer or examples — grep across the codebase finds no other reference.

Our actual OG components are OgImageLanding.satori.vue and OgImageDocs.satori.vue. The convention is 'defineOgImageComponent(<bareName>)' which strips the file's engine suffix (.satori.vue). Expected reference: 'OgImageLanding'.

Effect: landing pages currently fall back to nuxt-og-image's default OG rendering instead of using our custom OgImageLanding template.

Fix: change 'Frame' → 'OgImageLanding' (or rename the file to Landing.satori.vue and reference 'Landing' to match upstream convention).

title: Port docus markdown-rewrite (Vercel edge redirects for /raw/**.md)
description:
Port v5.5.0 #1264 from docus: layer/modules/markdown-rewrite.ts.

What it does: Vercel-only post-build module. Reads public/llms.txt, parses agent-discoverable URLs, and patches Vercel's config.json to add edge redirects so that requests with 'Accept: text/markdown' or 'User-Agent: curl/*' to a page URL are redirected to the corresponding /raw/<path>.md file.

Why deferred: orthogonal to the rendering architecture work in .1; Vercel-specific (will no-op on Railway/Docker); requires nuxt-llms to be generating llms.txt with /raw/* URLs.

When we adopt: add as layer/modules/markdown-rewrite/ following the upstream pattern. No nuxt-llms changes needed if our llms.txt already includes /raw/* URLs. Verify on a Vercel preview before merging.

title: Bump nuxt-og-image to v6 to enable ogImage.sitemap option
description:
Upstream docus v5.9.0 #1312 #1324 added 'ogImage: { sitemap: "/sitemap.xml" }' which forces static OG image generation per sitemap URL at build time.

Currently blocked: our active nuxt-og-image is v5.1.13 (via @nuxtjs/seo), which doesn't have the 'sitemap' module option. We also have v6.3.2 in node_modules from another transitive dep but it's not resolved by our layer.

Fix: either (a) pin nuxt-og-image to v6 in layer/package.json, or (b) bump @nuxtjs/seo to a version that bundles nuxt-og-image v6.

Risk: v6 may have other breaking changes. Verify by running build after bump.
notes:
Resolution (2026-05-20):

Attempted: pnpm update @nuxtjs/seo --latest, which bumped 5.1.0 → 5.1.3 and pulled nuxt-og-image v6.5.0 transitively.

Result: cascading peer-dep conflicts. The newer @nuxtjs/seo brings nuxt-seo-utils + nuxt-schema-org versions that depend on unhead@^3, while our other deps stay on unhead@^2. Also pulls h3@2.0.1-rc.11 alongside h3@1.15.11 already in tree, producing extensive H3Event type incompatibilities in our rss, mcp, and middleware modules.

Conclusion: this is a coordinated dep-bump task (unhead 2→3 + h3 1→2), not a single-package upgrade. Blocked behind that work.

Reverted layer/package.json and pnpm-lock.yaml; playground build still passes.
close_reason: Blocked: requires coordinated unhead 2→3 + h3 1→2 upgrade across the workspace; out of scope for this docus-sync epic
